title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 400 Security Holes
summary: Microsoft today released updates to remedy at least 398 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software, including one weakness that is already being actively exploited and two others that were publicly detailed prior to today.
card_summary: Microsoft today released updates to remedy at least 398 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software, including one weakness that is already being actively exploited and two others that were publicly detailed prior to today.
quick_take: Microsoft today released updates to remedy at least 398 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software, including one weakness that is already being actively exploited and two others…

sections.technical:
CVE-2026-62832 is another privilege escalation flaw that Microsoft has labeled likely to be exploited; this flaw, in the Windows User Profile Service, may be related to the recent LegacyHive public disclosure from the prolific bug hunter known as Nightmare Eclipse . The sole known zero day bug fixed by Microsoft this month is CVE-2026-68820 , a privilege escalation weakness in a core Windows component called afd.sys , which the security firm Automox describes as the driver behind Windows socket connections on effectively every endpoint. The other publicly disclosed flaw is CVE-2026-72971 , a low-impact local tampering vulnerability that Microsoft reckons is unlikely to be exploited. Fully 42 of the 398 flaws that Microsoft patched today earned Redmond s most-dire critical rating, meaning they are severe enough that malware or malcontents could exploit them to gain remote control over a Windows computer with little to no help from the user.

Referenced vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-62832, CVE-2026-68820, CVE-2026-72971.
sections.impact:
Microsoft has attributed the recent patch deluge to vulnerability discoveries aided by artificial intelligence, and experts roundly agree that Windows users should get used to the idea of Patch Tuesdays (the second Tuesday of each month) covering hundreds of newly discovered security flaws. Tyler Reguly at Fortra says while reports of Microsoft patching hundreds of vulnerabilities in one go has some organizations struggling to patch faster, it s important to bear in mind that only one of the almost 400 bugs addressed today is known to be actively exploited. Fully 42 of the 398 flaws that Microsoft patched today earned Redmond s most-dire critical rating, meaning they are severe enough that malware or malcontents could exploit them to gain remote control over a Windows computer with little to no help from the user.

Assessed severity: CRITICAL.
sections.mitigation: August s overstuffed bundle of patch joy from Microsoft did not eclipse its recording breaking release of more than 570 security updates last month , but it is double June s then-record batch of nearly 200 fixes . Microsoft has attributed the recent patch deluge to vulnerability discoveries aided by artificial intelligence, and experts roundly agree that Windows users should get used to the idea of Patch Tuesdays (the second Tuesday of each month) covering hundreds of newly discovered security flaws. But for now at least, patching the resulting bugpocalypse remains a heavily human-centric endeavor, and the jury is still out on whether AI technologies will turn out to be as good at fixing vulnerabilities as they are at finding and exploiting them. They found the LLMs produced patches that failed to fix the flaw or added a new weakness in the process (or both) more than half the time.
sections.context: This story is part of the recurring zero-day pattern where exploitation pressure is highest before broad patch adoption.

email_summary: Microsoft today released updates to remedy at least 398 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software, including one weakness that is already being actively exploited and two others that were publicly detailed prior to today. Tracked as CVE-2026-62832, CVE-2026-68820, CVE-2026-72971. Severity is rated critical.

title: A Malicious SIM Card Can Run Attacker Code Inside the Modems Behind Cellular IoT Devices
